classification.difficultyReason: Sketch eighteen linear half-planes, rearranging some inequalities and distinguishing included from excluded boundaries.

answer.short: Shade above the dashed line $y=x+1$; exclude the line.
answer.worked: Draw the boundary $y=x+1$ through $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Use a dashed line because the inequality is strict. Shade above the line.

spec.description: Dashed boundary through the two intercepts; required upper half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade below the dashed line $y=2x+3$; exclude the line.
answer.worked: Draw $y=2x+3$ through $(-\tfrac32,0)$ and $(0,3)$. Use a dashed boundary. The point $(0,0)$ satisfies $0<3$, so shade the side containing the origin.

spec.description: Dashed boundary and shaded lower half-plane.

answer.short: Shade below the solid line $y=2x-1$, including the line.
answer.worked: Draw $y=2x-1$ through $(\tfrac12,0)$ and $(0,-1)$. Use a solid boundary because equality is included. Shade below it.

spec.description: Solid boundary and shaded lower half-plane.

answer.short: Shade above the dashed line $y=1-x$; exclude the line.
answer.worked: Draw $y=1-x$ through $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$. Use a dashed boundary and shade above it.

spec.description: Dashed descending boundary and shaded upper half-plane.

answer.short: Shade below the solid line $y=4-2x$, including the line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x+y&\le4\\y&\le4-2x\end{align*}$$
Draw the solid boundary through $(0,4)$ and $(2,0)$. Shade below it; the origin satisfies the inequality.

spec.description: Solid descending boundary; lower half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade below the dashed line $y=\tfrac32x-3$; exclude the line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3x-2y&>6\\-2y&>6-3x\\y&<\tfrac32x-3\end{align*}$$
Dividing by $-2$ reverses the inequality. Draw the dashed boundary through $(0,-3)$ and $(2,0)$ and shade below it.

spec.description: Dashed rising boundary; lower half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade above the dashed line $y=1-3x$; exclude the line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3x+y&>1\\y&>1-3x\end{align*}$$
Draw the dashed boundary through $(0,1)$ and $(\tfrac13,0)$. Shade above it.

spec.description: Dashed descending boundary; upper half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade above the dashed line $y=\tfrac12x-\tfrac12$; exclude the line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x-2y&<1\\-2y&<1-x\\y&>\tfrac12x-\tfrac12\end{align*}$$
Dividing by $-2$ reverses the inequality. Draw the dashed boundary through $(0,-\tfrac12)$ and $(1,0)$ and shade above it.

spec.description: Dashed rising boundary; upper half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade below the solid line $y=2x$, including the line.
answer.worked: Draw the solid boundary $y=2x$ through $(0,0)$ and $(1,2)$. Shade below it.

spec.description: Solid boundary through the origin and labelled point (1,2); lower half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade above the solid line $y=3x$, including the line.
answer.worked: Draw the solid boundary $y=3x$ through $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-3)$. Shade above it.

spec.description: Solid boundary through the origin and labelled point (-1,-3); upper half-plane shaded.
spec.mathematics: y>=3x; equal coordinate units preserve the mathematical gradient.

answer.short: Shade right of the solid vertical line $x=3$, including the line.
answer.worked: Draw the vertical boundary $x=3$ as a solid line. Values of $x$ greater than $3$ lie to its right, so shade that side and include the boundary.

spec.description: Solid vertical boundary at x=3, shaded to the right.

answer.short: Shade left of the dashed vertical line $x=1$; exclude the line.
answer.worked: Draw the vertical boundary $x=1$ as a dashed line. Shade to its left because the required points have $x<1$.

spec.description: Dashed vertical boundary at x=1, shaded to the left.

answer.short: Shade below the dashed horizontal line $y=2$; exclude the line.
answer.worked: Draw the horizontal boundary $y=2$ as a dashed line. Shade below it because the required points have $y<2$.

spec.description: Dashed horizontal boundary at y=2, shaded below.

answer.short: Shade below the solid horizontal line $y=-2$, including the line.
answer.worked: Draw the horizontal boundary $y=-2$ as a solid line. Shade below it and include the boundary because equality is allowed.

spec.description: Solid horizontal boundary at y=-2, shaded below.

answer.short: Shade below the solid line $y=4-\tfrac43x$, including the line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4x+3y&\le12\\3y&\le12-4x\\y&\le4-\tfrac43x\end{align*}$$
Draw the solid boundary through $(0,4)$ and $(3,0)$. Shade below it; the origin satisfies the inequality.

spec.description: Solid descending boundary; lower half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade above the solid line $y=2x-8$, including the line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x-y&\le8\\-y&\le8-2x\\y&\ge2x-8\end{align*}$$
Multiplying by $-1$ reverses the inequality. Draw the solid boundary through $(0,-8)$ and $(4,0)$ and shade above it.

spec.description: Solid rising boundary with both intercepts visible; upper half-plane shaded.
spec.mathematics: y>=2x-8; intercepts (0,-8),(4,0). Axis units differ and labelled intercepts establish the scales.

answer.short: Shade below the solid line $y=2x-4$, including the line.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x-y&\ge4\\-y&\ge4-2x\\y&\le2x-4\end{align*}$$
Multiplying by $-1$ reverses the inequality. Draw the solid boundary through $(0,-4)$ and $(2,0)$ and shade below it.

spec.description: Solid rising boundary; lower half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade below the dashed line $y=3-2x$; exclude the line.
answer.worked: Draw $y=3-2x$ through $(0,3)$ and $(\tfrac32,0)$. Use a dashed boundary and shade below it. The origin satisfies $0<3$.

spec.description: Dashed descending boundary; lower half-plane shaded.
